description:
Stories by Industry/Location
News stories about an industry and/or a place, e.g. biotech deals in Texas. Use this when there is no specific company in mind; for news about a named company use `stories_organization_list`. Pass `industry` (plain words, e.g. "biotech") or `industry_id` (from `industry_clusters_list`), and/or `activity_location` (from `location_groups_list`): at least one is required. Returns `{count, next, previous, results, data_last_updated}`, plus `payment` on a call paid with x402: what it cost (`amount` in `currency` on `network`), whether it was `free`, and `free_calls_remaining` during a promotion. Each result is one story, newest first, with `activity_class` (its type), `label`, `headline`, `document_extract`, `published_date`, `published_by`, `document_url` and `uri`. 20 results per page by default (`page_size` up to 100); follow `next` or pass `page` for more. Use `stories_retrieve` with a story's `uri` for its full detail (people, organizations and places involved, by role). Filter by story type with `type` and by recency with `days_ago` (7, 30 or 90 days; default 90). If the response is HTTP 202 the same query is already being computed: retry after the Retry-After seconds. Syracuse leaves out stories it isn't confident about, so empty `results` means nothing trustworthy was found; such a call, like an error or a 202, is free and doesn't count against the API key's quota. Payment: an API key, or $0.02 per call in USDC on Base via x402, charged only when the call returns results; first 50 calls per wallet free from 30 November to 7 December 2026. Terms: https://syracuse.1145.am/terms

activity_location.description: Location group name or id (e.g. "texas", "india", "MidWest", "FR", "us-ca") where the story happened. Not case sensitive. Accepts multiple values. They must each match an id or name from the location groups endpoint (`/api/v1/location-groups/`, MCP tool `location_groups_list`).

activity_location_id.description: Location group identifiers (e.g., "Southern Asia", "BT", "US-CA") where the story happened. Case-sensitive. Accepts multiple values. They must each match an id from the location groups endpoint (`/api/v1/location-groups/`, MCP tool `location_groups_list`).

days_ago.description:
How far back to look, in days: 7, 30 or 90. Counted back from the date the data was last updated (the `data_last_updated` field in the response), not from today. Defaults to 90.

* `7` - 7
* `30` - 30
* `90` - 90

include_provenance.description: Add a `source_audit` field to each story explaining why it matched (which source it came from, its match score, and the entity that carried it). Defaults to false.

industry.description: Industry name to filter by, in plain words (e.g. "biotech", "cybersecurity"). Matched by meaning, so no exact name is needed. Accepts multiple values.

industry_context.description: Optional context aspects to anchor the industry search in. Pass each aspect as a separate value. Can be a broader category name or detailed examples (e.g. "Movie Industry" when searching for "Distribution", or "BOPP Film" and "BOPET Film" when searching for "Film"). Applied to every value of `industry` in the same request.

industry_id.description: Industry ID (topic ID) to filter by. Accepts multiple values. They must each match a topic_id from the industry clusters endpoint (`/api/v1/industry-clusters/`, MCP tool `industry_clusters_list`).

output.description: Output format. Defaults to "simple" (SimpleStory schema). Use "full" for the detailed response.

page.description: A page number within the paginated result set.

page_size.description: Number of results to return per page.

type.description: Only return stories of these types. Accepts multiple values; omit for all types. Values: IndustrySectorUpdate (Analyst or market-report findings about an industry sector rather than one company); CorporateFinanceActivity (M&A, investments, stock purchases); PartnershipActivity (Partnership between 2 or more organizations. Often, companies describe their customers as their partners. This type of activity covers both genuine partnerships and customer/supplier relationships); RoleActivity (Key change in senior personnel, e.g. replacing CEO); LocationActivity (Opening or closing a new location (e.g. setting up in EMEA or shutting down a factory in a particular town)); ProductActivity (New product launches); AnalystRatingActivity (Updates from industry analysts); EquityActionsActivity (Stock repurchases, dividends etc); FinancialReportingActivity (Notice that an organization is going to announce its financials); FinancialsActivity (Information about company financials, e.g. revenue or EBITDA); IncidentActivity (Adverse incidents e.g. safety); LegalActivity (Lawsuits or activities that could lead to lawsuits, e.g. SEC investigations); MarketingActivity (e.g. launching a new advertising campaign); OperationsActivity (Company operations news, e.g. we are investing in a new product, or we have just completed an security audit); RecognitionActivity (e.g. we are delighted to announce that we won Agency of the Year); RegulatoryActivity (Legal or regulatory activity affecting this organization, e.g. permit for drilling, or regulatory filing); IndustryEventActivity (Conferences, trade shows, award ceremonies and similar events an organization hosts or takes part in).
